description.purpose: The window of one model, owned in one place, with a ledger of every call. The hive decides the whole context of the model it serves -- the system part, the history and the running round -- and writes down, per call, exactly which blocks went out: every element is stored once under the sha256 of its canonical JSON, the wall records the order they arrived in, and `calls` plus `call_blocks` rebuild any request byte for byte. The system part is sent only when a family of it changed, and then as one `$replace` root; between two rebuilds only the end of the window moves, which is what a provider's prefix cache keys on. When the model reports that its cache has gone cold, or the prompt crosses `compress_at` of the context window, a small model of the hive's own condenses the older history into one summary, which the window then carries as `system.history.summary` -- never while a call waits, at most one at a time, and a failed summary leaves the window as it was. Since 1.1.0 ([#892](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/892), [#893](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/893), [#895](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/895), [#896](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/896)) the window follows a role (`role`: `talky`, `consult`, `coding`, `research`), foreign words and tool results stand behind a short id `[#<12 hex>]` the model can release or pin through the `window` section of its answer, another hive can pin a text into the window (`in_pin`), and the hive answers the collector's menu question itself (`./schemas`); `./history` answers the `history_*` tools out of the ledger, `./push` builds the memory leg's question and looks a `gap` up after the answer, and `./handover` hands a new session a note on the last one and a renewed duplex call a block of the recent conversation. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.1.1 ([#904](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/904)) the cache clock is one standing order under a fixed id per hive, re-armed on every call (`add` with `rearm`), so the timer keeps one row for it instead of one per call; a repair, so it is the third digit. Since 1.3.0 ([#925](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/925), [#926](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/926), [#931](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/931)) every ledger row carries `audience_set`, the audience of the round that caused it, and every reader serves a row only to a round that lies within it; a history tool called without a round is answered `missing_audience`, the window and the handover of a round-less call take only the running session's rows that declare no round either, a pin without a round is refused, the ledger marks a tool error, a clarifying question and a rewritten standing instruction once each, and `./stats` answers `in_stats` with counts of the hive's own ledger on `stats`. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.4.0 ([#932](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/932), [#935](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/935)) every reader selects its rows through the store's `covers` operator, so a round reads only the rows it may see and never learns how many it may not; a row written without a round carries `[]`; `hop.turn_id` counts per round as `<session>#<tag>-<index>`; the knob `identity_budget` (`full` or `split`) decides whether the identity goes whole into every call or whole once and short after it; and the pack takes a fifth family, `identity_short`. A caller can do what it could not before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.4.1 ([#941](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/941)) the model call carries `hop.episode_turn_id`, the id `turn_write` gives the person's episode of that turn, so a reader of a sidecar section can address the episode; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.5.0 ([#943](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/943)) `./policy` keeps one window plan per round under its `round_key` rather than one per hive, bounded by the params `max_round_plans` and `round_plan_idle_s`. Params joined, so it is the second digit. Since 1.6.0 ([#949](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/949)) another part of the colony hands the curator candidates on `in_candidate` (acknowledged on `candidate_ack` when asked for), and the live ones a turn covers are pushed into the round's wall within a budget; with `things_section` on, the section `things` leaves as `thing_seen` under the round it was drawn in; and `./reader` answers `in_read` with the turns and sessions the caller's round may see. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.7.0 ([#972](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/972), [#955](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/955)) a pin carries the round its row proves: `turn_round` and the edge round bound it, a pin no round can prove stays `pin:held`, all audience groups of one source travel in one message, and two first rebuild claims of the same round leave exactly one winner. A caller can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.7.1 ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) `./summarizer` declares the optional hop key `dropped`, the sampling fields a model's `supported_params` left out; nothing else moved. Since 1.7.2 ([#999](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/999)) `./summarizer` declares the optional hop key `unverified`, the sampling fields sent without a `supported_params` list to check them; nothing else moved. Since 1.9.0 ([#1038](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1038)) `./policy` knows what its window costs: with the answering model's limits and prices on the tap (`input_soft`, `input_hard`, `cost_in`, `cost_cached_in`, stamped by the llm cell) a rebuild is due at the soft limit, over the hard one, and under soft when the cached rest over `amortise_turns` turns costs more than one rebuild; every turn stamps its window, cache share, cost estimate and `curate_mark`. New behaviour and a new param, so it is the second digit. Since 1.10.0 ([#1040](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1040)) the memory ask carries the answering model's package: `./policy` keeps the `input_soft` of the last answer, cut to the usable window (state `input_soft`), and `./push` hands it on every ask it builds as `recall_input_soft` and grows the role's preset `recall_budget` by the memory hive's query factor (at most twice; a budget the instance set stays as set). A consumer can read a key it never could, so it is the second digit. Since 1.10.1 ([#1044](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1044)) every model call carries `hop.recall_input_soft` (state `input_soft`, the usable window `./push` hands the memory), so the parent can stamp it on the model's own `memory_recall`, and an ask `./push` hands on untouched (`recall_push` off) carries it too, read from state on its way through; it repairs the #1040 promise, so it is the third digit. Since 1.11.0 ([#1079](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1079)) `./intake` checks a sidecar section the parent names in `hop.sidecar_verify` before it hands it on: each quoted field of each item is looked up word for word (normal form: NFC, casefold, unified quotes and dashes, collapsed whitespace) in the turns of the round (`turn`), plus the round's recall (`turn+recall`) or in the answer (`answer`); an item that fails is dropped (or marked, `mode: mark`) and one `reject` per failed item leaves with `reject_reason` `quote_missing` or `quote_not_in_source`, never with the quoted text. A new emitted route, so it is the second digit. Since 1.11.1 ([#801](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/801)) its summarizer takes the provider key as a sealed vault grant (`credential_grant_id`, asked on `credential_request`, answered on `in_sealed`) instead of `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the process environment; a literal key in the instance still works for 0.62.x while no grant is set. Where a key comes from is a repair of the promise, so it is the third digit.Since 1.11.2 (GH #1085, R-IG-1) the hive is the one place that cuts what its model reads, by shares of the window of the model that reads it (the catalog's `input_soft`) and never by a typed number: an earlier answer's sidecar block, the collector's sidecar contract (its frame written anew over the sections kept), the handover block, the push candidates and a `history_read` by the served window (the model's catalog row); the summarizer's and the handover note's transcripts by the summarizer's own window (the stamp on its answers, the bound of a refusal, before either the catalogue row in `input_soft_fallback`); a page of `./reader` by the asker's. Without a known window everything goes whole and, over its share, carries a mark naming what was shown of how much (`...[cut: <shown> of <total> chars shown; <hint>]`, `...[dropped: <name> (<n> chars) over budget]`), each cut also on the hop as `cuts`; a find said aloud and the summary go whole (the model's words; the summarizer is asked to keep it as short as useful and as long as needed); a pin and a summary are refused only over the carrier's system leaf (4 MiB without a window, the window's own bound with one); every ask of a producer carries `input_soft`. The knobs `sidecar_max_chars`, `handover_chars`, `read_budget` (reader, history), `candidate_budget`, `summary_budget` and `summary_chars` are gone (`candidate_push` switches the candidates). A repair of the boundary's promise, so it is the third digit. Since 1.11.3 ([#1085](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1085)) no role types a window of its own: `quality_cap` (talky 120000, consult 80000, coding 70000, research 80000 tokens, GH #892) is gone from the presets, the params and the settings, so the usable window is the answering model's catalog row (`input_soft`), cut only to the model's own reported window, and the rebuild lines, every share and `recall_input_soft` follow from it -- a talky under luna rebuilds at the row's lines, not at 60000 tokens. A repair of the promise of R-IG-1, so it is the third digit. Since 1.11.4 ([#1094](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1094)) `./summarizer` keeps its contract on the `credential_request` route: `finish_reason` is required on every answer but optional on that route, which carries only the grant. Without it a colony that validates emissions dropped the request as `contract_violation`; a contract that admits what the cell already sends is a repair, so it is the third digit.
description.use_when: In front of any `llm` cell whose window must not grow without bound or must be accountable: instantiate it with `ctx.model` for its summarizer, send the round on `in_curate`, draw `brain` onto the model with `curator_call`, `session_id`, `turn_id` and `iter` promoted into context, and route every output of the model back on `in_llm` with that context. The model's `system_order` puts `history` after `identity`, `persona` and `instructions`, so the summary is the last and least stable part of the system prompt.
description.not_in_scope: No retrieval and no tool round of its own: the caller gathers, this hive keeps and projects -- the one tool family it answers is the model's own wall (`history_*`). No judgement of what is true: a summary reports what was said. It never parses a sidecar block: the parent's splitter cuts it and hands the curator its own sections (`window`, `gap`, `memory`) on `in_section`.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed; a mutation edge onto a cell inside is refused with hive_port_boundary). Entry: in_curate, in_slots, in_llm, in_pack, in_close, in_model, in_section, in_pin, in_schemas, in_history_call, in_recall_ask, in_gap_bundle, in_renewed, in_stats. Exit on `hop.route`: brain, turn_write, write, pack_ack, model_refused, sidecar, tool_schemas, tool_result, recall, stats.

LEDGER - `blocks` (hash, kind, chars, body, first_seen), `wall` (seq, session_id, turn_id, iter, kind, hash, nth, final, episode_idx, at), `calls`, `call_blocks`, `summaries`, `slots`, `state`, `marks` (seq, session_id, turn_id, kind, value, at), `pins` (hash, source, until, at). A call is rebuilt by reading its `call_blocks` in `pos` order and each block's `body`: the system leaves first, then the messages.

REBUILD - a tap stamped `cache_expires_at` sets the clock (one standing order, re-armed for this call); when it fires for the newest call, the wall between the last summary and the newest `keep_recent` rounds goes to the summarizer with the previous summary, and the next call's `actions` name `rebuild:cache` and the summary id.

ROLE - `./policy` `role` `talky`: today raw, yesterday one summary, older nothing, the newest 40 rounds raw, short ids `[#<12 hex>]` on somebody else's words and tool results; the model's `window` section releases ids (one line from the next rebuild on, `history_read` brings them back) or pins them.

HISTORY - the model reads its own wall (GH #893): `history_search` (phrase, exact or regex, newest first, `#<12 hex>` ids with excerpts), `history_read` (a block by its id or a turn range, whole or refused `too_large`), `history_outline` (sessions and their topics). The parent routes `hop.tool_name` starting `history_` to `in_history_call` and takes `tool_result` into its collector's `in_tool`.

HANDOVER - a closed session leaves a note written by the summarizer off the hot path; the first call of a NEW session carries it as `system.history.handover` with the topic still open (without a close: the topic alone, put together without a model), and a renewed live session of a running call gets the conversation so far -- turns, summary, pins, topic -- as a `sidecar` section `context` at once (GH #896).

model.because: the model the summarizer condenses the history with
